title: Multi-armed canary experiment framework with automated rollback and root-cause tagging
creator: Samira Khan
description:
Background: As model and serving config churn increases, our current canary tooling detects single-metric regressions but struggles with multi-dimensional quality shifts that affect a subset of prompts. We need a framework that treats canary and multi-arm A/B rollouts as formal experiments: sample selection, counterfactual comparison, multi-metric arbitration, and an automated, auditable rollback when the hypothesis ("new variant is not worse") is rejected.

Goals: 1) Detect quality regressions across multiple metrics (semantic correctness, hallucination prevalence, token-level edit distance for golden tests, latency P95, and error rate) within a tight time window for small cohorts. 2) Provide automated rollback orchestration with clear provenance and root-cause tags to accelerate postmortems. 3) Surface diagnostics and individual sample diffs in Console for triage.

Proposal: Implement a "Multi-Armed Canary Experiment" subsystem with these components:
- Experiment Controller: Kubernetes-native controller that owns lifecycle of experiments (create, scale, abort, finalize).
- Shadowing & Sampling: mirror a percentage of production requests to candidate variants (true counterfactual) with deterministic sampling keys for reproducibility.
- Aggregation Pipeline: per-request metric enrichment (eval hooks) that emits labeled metrics to the experiment store.
- Decision Engine: configurable arbitration engine that supports multiple statistical tests (two-sided bootstrap for deltas, Bayesian posterior checks) and a weighted rule layer to combine metrics into a pass/fail decision. Hysteresis and min-sample thresholds to avoid flips on noise.
- Rollback Orchestrator: when Decision Engine triggers a fail, call routing API to rollback traffic (percentage-step or immediate) and open an incident record with root-cause tags and a snapshot of failing sample diffs.
- Visibility & Controls: Console panels for experiment health, per-metric deltas, p-values, sample inspector, and a runbook link. Alerts into Slack and PagerDuty when automated rollback occurs.

Trade-offs & constraints: Start with a conservative default policy (small cohort sizes, strict min-samples, require 2 metrics to exceed thresholds) to avoid false positives. The Decision Engine will be pluggable so we can iterate on statistical method (bootstrap vs Bayesian). This work depends on incremental eval hooks in the SDK (see dependencies).

Security & Audit: All rollback activities logged with request provenance. If a customer requests air-gapped behavior, the controller can be disabled; this is treated as a deployment flag.

Success criteria: faster detection and mitigation of regressions, shorter MTTI/MTTR for rollout incidents, fewer manual reverts by SRE/PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Create experiment controller with CRUD and experiment state transitions visible in Console
Wire shadowing so candidate variants receive deterministic mirrored requests without impacting production latencies
Implement aggregation pipeline that emits per-request eval metrics (semantic score, hallucination flag, latency) to experiment store within 60s
Decision Engine implements at least two statistical tests and a configurable rule to combine metric signals
Automated rollback orchestrator can revert a variant and record an incident with sample diffs and tags
Console dashboard shows per-metric delta, cohort size, p-values, and a sample inspector for at least two recent experiments
E2E test coverage for abort, fail-triggered rollback, and manual override paths
Runbook for on-call that explains automated rollback incident flow and steps to disable an experiment
